title: What Is SLED Contracting?
description: Learn what SLED contracting means, which public buyers it can include, and why state, local, and education procurement should be approached as a distinct market.

sections.heading: SLED is a practical market label
paragraphs: SLED is commonly used as shorthand for state, local, and education public-sector markets. In practice, that can include state agencies, counties, cities, towns, school districts, public colleges and universities, authorities, and other eligible public institutions.

The term is useful for business development because these buyers often operate outside federal procurement notice systems. A company monitoring only federal opportunities can therefore miss a large category of public-sector purchasing activity.

sections.heading: SLED procurement is distributed across many buyers
paragraphs: There is no single universal portal covering every state, county, city, school, university, and authority. Businesses typically need to learn which procurement systems are used by the jurisdictions and institutions they want to serve.

NASPO maintains procurement profiles for individual states. Those profiles are useful starting points for understanding state procurement organizations, while local governments and educational institutions may maintain separate systems and vendor-registration processes.

sections.heading: Some state and local buyers can also use GSA programs
paragraphs: GSA identifies state, county, local, town, city, tribal, territorial, public-school, college, university, and similar eligible entities for certain state and local purchasing programs. Cooperative Purchasing, Disaster Purchasing, the 1122 program, and Public Health Emergency purchasing each have their own eligibility and scope.

Those federal purchasing channels do not replace a state or locality's own procurement rules. GSA guidance notes that buyers using grant money must still follow applicable local procurement regulations and granting-agency requirements.

sections.heading: Build a SLED search strategy around geography and buyer type
paragraphs: A practical SLED strategy begins with the places where a business can realistically deliver. From there, identify the state agencies, municipalities, counties, educational institutions, and authorities that purchase the relevant products or services.

Track registrations, portal accounts, commodity classifications, recurring buyers, and solicitation calendars. Then evaluate each opportunity for scope, capacity, schedule, terms, and response effort rather than treating every public notice as equally valuable.
